title: How do you write a number as Tens plus Ones?
description: Tanvi packs pencils for the school. The video writes two numbers as Tens or Hundreds plus Ones by taking away what the Tens or Hundreds cover.
teaching_notes: One idea: take away the value of the Tens or Hundreds, and what is left is the Ones. Watch for the last digit being used as the Ones.

source: Write 983 as 90 Tens + __ Ones, and 4,560 as 45 Hundreds + _
video_script.why: The child knows place value but has not yet regrouped a number into Tens or Hundreds plus the rest as Ones.
video_script.substitution: Find the value of the given Tens or Hundreds, take it away from the number, and what is left is the Ones.
video_script.anchor: Tanvi packing pencils into boxes for the school
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says three Ones because the last digit of nine hundred and eighty-three is three. Ninety Tens are only nine hundred, so more than three is left over.
video_script.payoff_line: take away the tens, and what is left is the ones

final_answer.spoken: ninety Tens plus eighty-three Ones, and forty-five Hundreds plus sixty Ones

maths_rules: slip: using the last digit gives 90 Tens + 3 Ones = 903, not 983
your turn: 764 = 60 Tens + 164 Ones; 3,280 = 30 Hundreds + 280 Ones; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: take away the Tens or Hundreds and the rest is Ones. Wrong idea: the last digit is the Ones. A tray for leftover Ones stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='pack'/>Tanvi packs pencils for the school. One box has nine hundred and eighty-three pencils. Another box has four thousand, five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write nine hundred and eighty-three as ninety Tens plus some Ones. Write four thousand, five hundred and sixty as forty-five Hundreds plus some Ones.

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>One Ten is worth ten Ones, and ninety Tens are worth nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='hun'/>One Hundred is worth one hundred, and forty-five Hundreds are worth four thousand, five hundred.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Anything the Tens or the Hundreds do not cover is counted in Ones.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Three Ones, because the last digit is three.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>The three is only the last digit of the number.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Ninety Tens are nine hundred, and more is left over.

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Ninety Tens make nine hundred. Take nine hundred away from nine hundred and eighty-three.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Take away the tens, and what is left is the ones.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Eighty-three is left, so nine hundred and eighty-three is ninety Tens plus eighty-three Ones.

marks.ans: the answer 45 Hundreds + 60 Ones is written

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Forty-five Hundreds make four thousand, five hundred.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Take that away from four thousand, five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Sixty is left, so four thousand, five hundred and sixty is forty-five Hundreds plus sixty Ones.
